around.headline: CBI raids 12 locations across Bengaluru, Mumbai and Pune over an alleged builder-financial institution nexus
around.summary: The CBI searched 12 locations in Bengaluru, Mumbai and Pune in connection with an alleged nexus between builders and financial institutions, per Deccan Herald and The Hans India. Worth being extra careful verifying a builder's and lender's credentials before signing any property loan or investment.

around.summary: Private bus operators have raised fares ahead of the Ganesh Chaturthi travel rush, per Public TV English — book early or compare with railway special trains if you're heading out of the city this week.

around.headline: BBMP rolls out 'jet patcher' machines to fix potholes on busy roads
around.summary: Bengaluru is deploying new jet-patcher technology to repair potholes on high-traffic roads, per Rediff and The Siasat Daily — a faster fix than manual patching, so expect fewer pothole complaints on covered stretches soon.

around.headline: Hebbal tunnel project draws concern over groundwater and flooding risk
around.summary: Experts and citizens are raising concerns that Bengaluru's Hebbal tunnel road project could disrupt groundwater flow and worsen local flooding, per Mongabay India — worth watching if you live or commute near the route ahead of heavy rain.

around.headline: NSE IPO price band set at Rs 1,700-1,785, opens September 17
around.summary: The National Stock Exchange has fixed its IPO price band at Rs 1,700-1,785 per share, with the issue opening September 17, per IndiaInfoline — one to watch if you're a retail investor planning to apply.

around.headline: Modi and Putin agree to strengthen the India-Russia partnership ahead of the BRICS summit
around.summary: Ahead of the BRICS summit in New Delhi, Modi and Putin agreed to strengthen the India-Russia partnership, per Reuters — talks continue this week as the summit brings Xi Jinping and other global leaders to the capital.

street_smart.title: You're selling your old laptop on OLX. A buyer comes over, says he's just paid via UPI, and shows you a screenshot on his phone reading 'Payment Successful — Rs 18,000' with a transaction ID. He's in a hurry and asks you to hand over the laptop right now. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: No single news item today mapped cleanly to an individual scam trap, so this draws on the evergreen rotation — UPI fraud and fake payment screenshots hasn't come up as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks, and fits today's CBI story on financial-nexus fraud as a reminder that financial trust needs verifying, not just seeing.
street_smart.situation: He's checking his watch, saying he has somewhere to be, and gestures for you to pack up the laptop while he 'waits for the SMS confirmation.'

choices.text: Open your own bank app or wait for your bank's SMS/notification to confirm the money has actually landed in your account before handing over the laptop; if it hasn't, ask him to wait.
choices.feedback: Correct. A screenshot is just an image — fake UPI-lookalike apps and simple photo edits can produce a convincing 'Payment Successful' screen in seconds. Only your own bank's confirmation (SMS, app balance, or passbook) proves money actually moved.

choices.text: Accept the screenshot as proof since it shows a transaction ID and a 'Payment Successful' message, and hand over the laptop right away.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Screenshots — even with transaction IDs — can be faked or come from apps designed to mimic real payment confirmations. Sellers who hand over goods based on a screenshot alone are a classic target for this scam.

choices.text: Tell him to instead send a UPI 'collect request' for the amount, since that feels more official and trackable, and approve it on your phone.
choices.feedback: Risky — actually dangerous. A UPI collect request asks YOU to pay, not the buyer to pay you. Approving one in a hurry, thinking it's a receipt confirmation, is one of the most common ways people lose money in these exact face-to-face 'sale' scams.

choices.text: Let him take the laptop now since he seems genuine and in a rush, and follow up by phone later if the payment hasn't reflected.
choices.feedback: Risky. Once the item and the buyer are gone, you have no leverage — a phone that goes unanswered later is far more likely than a delayed credit showing up on its own.

takeaways: Never release goods on the strength of a screenshot — always verify the actual credit in your own bank app, SMS alert, or passbook first.
Never approve a UPI 'collect request' from someone claiming to pay you — collect requests pull money out of your account, they don't put money in.
For in-person cash-equivalent deals, cash or a verified real-time bank transfer (checked on your own device) is safer than trusting anything shown on the other person's phone.

quiz.question: How many locations did the CBI search across Bengaluru, Mumbai and Pune over the alleged builder-financial institution nexus?
quiz.why: The searches targeted an alleged nexus between builders and financial institutions — a reminder to verify credentials before signing property loans or investments.

quiz.question: Karnataka's government has now limited the singing of Vande Mataram at government functions to how many stanzas, barring VVIP events?
quiz.why: The order applies to routine government functions; VVIP events are exempt from the restriction, per TOI Bengaluru.

quiz.question: Ahead of the BRICS summit in New Delhi this week, what did Modi and Putin agree to strengthen?
quiz.why: The talks came on the eve of the summit, which is also bringing Xi Jinping and other world leaders to Delhi, per Reuters.

quiz.question: Bengaluru draws most of its municipal drinking water from which river, pumped over 100 km uphill into the city?
quiz.why: Water is lifted from the Cauvery near T.K. Halli and pumped uphill in stages — one reason Bengaluru's water supply is so energy-intensive compared to cities on a riverbank.

quiz.question: What causes Earth's greenhouse effect, which keeps the planet warm enough to sustain life?
options: Gases like CO2 absorbing and re-emitting infrared heat in the atmosphere
Volcanic ash blocking heat from escaping
quiz.why: Without any greenhouse effect at all, Earth's average surface temperature would be well below freezing — the same mechanism, intensified by extra CO2, is what drives modern climate change.
